Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who confirmed the deaths, called the crash a “horrific tragedy.”
Sunday’s incident is the worst crash involving a Learjet 60, according to data from the Flight Safety Foundation. In 2008, four were killed when a Learjet 60 bound for Los Angeles crashed on takeoff from Columbia, South Carolina.
The plane was a Learjet 60 flying to the Bahamas from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. It is registered to an LLC in Delaware, according to FAA records, and is listed as available for charter online.
The FAA and NTSB will investigate the crash, the FAA said.
NTSB investigators will arrive at the site Sunday and Monday. A news conference is also planned for Monday.
The crash occurred near Military Trail, between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement.
Minutes before the crash, the pilot of the plane reported ice accumulating on the aircraft, an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius, and moderate turbulence, bouncing the plane by up to 700 feet, according to a recording of air traffic control radio calls captured by LiveATC.net.
“We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence,” the pilot radioed the Miami Air Route Traffic Control Center.
But moments later, after reporting precipitation started to fall and requesting to climb, they declared an emergency.
“We’re descending 8,000 – mayday, mayday – we’re descending 10,000 feet per minute,” the pilot said. “We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute … We’re going to crash into the ground.”
The jet descended 27,000 feet over the course of one minute, just before flight tracking data cut off, the website ADS-B Exchange shows.
The road is buckled where the plane slammed into it, creating a crater, video from CNN affiliate WPBF showed.
About 600 people are in need shelter after the plane crash because of the damage on the ground, said Joel Flores, Palm Beach County commissioner for District 3, who was the first county official at the scene. The residents are being sent to two shelters in the county while the site is being investigated, he said.
“I heard and felt the boom,” Andrew Mannino told CNN. “The power immediately went out and is still out.”
He said he smelled the smoke and “saw a large black cloud immerse in the air.”
The crash site is about four miles south of the airport in West Palm Beach, which was renamed for President Donald Trump earlier this year. Trump was in West Palm Beach earlier Sunday, but departed the airport on Air Force One a little more than one hour before this crash.
Dash cam video showing the crash is going to be important to investigators piecing together what happened, said Mary Schiavo, CNN aviation analyst and former inspector general for the Transportation Department.
The airport is a good place to wait out the bad weather, Schiavo told CNN’s Fredricka Whitfield Sunday. “That is not a controlled descent. That is a descent where literally you’re exceeding that the speed of the plane on descent. You’re exceeding the descent rate. So at that point, it’s clear whatever happened, they had lost control of the plane.”
The steep descent could have taken parts off the plane, and the flight recorder could have been destroyed in the explosion, Schiavo added.
There were scattered storms in the area at the time of the crash, and the plane passed through a stronger storm cell a few minutes before it began descending. It is unclear if the storm contributed to the crash but at the time, the flight was in an area where the FAA had warned of thunderstorms and threats to aircraft, known as a convective SIGMET.
Ice on wings and other surfaces can pose a major threat to private jets. In January 2024, the NTSB published a safety alert underscoring the risks of in-flight icing conditions, which can cause pilots to lose control. The agency warned ice can “make managing the airplane’s flightpath and airspeed more difficult and can prevent the airplane from maintaining level flight.”
All northbound and southbound lanes of Military Trail are closed until further notice, officials said, and motorists are advised to avoid the area and seek alternate routes.

sources.text:
All nine people aboard a private Learjet 60 died in Sunday’s Palm Beach County crash, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said, according to the Associated Press. WATCH: Video captures the Palm Beach County jet crash
Viewer discretion advised: this video shows a fatal crash and fire. The BNO News post is embedded below. Mediaite’s coverage also identifies footage shared by local station CBS12, including recordings of the impact and aftermath. The images provide a view of the disaster from the ground. They cannot resolve what was happening aboard the aircraft or substitute for a formal investigation. Some early video captions were written before officials announced the fatalities.
A Bahamas-bound flight ends in Florida
The FAA says the Learjet 60 left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. It crashed in a residential area near Cresthaven at approximately 12:50 p.m. local time. Nine people were aboard. The agency describes these details as preliminary and says the National Transportation Safety Board will lead the investigation. The crash location should not be confused with the aircraft’s intended destination.
What is known about the aircraft
An Austin airport spokesperson identified the aircraft as N722BD in AP reporting carried by the San Francisco Chronicle. The FAA registry entry lists that registration as a Learjet 60, serial number 271, registered to LR60271 LLC in Wilmington, Delaware. A registered owner is not a passenger list, and it does not establish who was operating or traveling on a particular flight. The registry itself warns that its information is not a basis for determining airworthiness. We have not independently confirmed the victims’ identities or a passenger-and-crew breakdown.
The neighborhood response and unanswered casualty questions
NBC6’s developing coverage reports a fireball, smoke and a road closure along Military Trail between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North. Authorities asked motorists to take another route. Whether anyone on the ground was injured remained unclear in the reporting reviewed for this article. That distinction matters: confirmation that everyone aboard died does not establish that no one else was harmed. It also does not establish additional deaths. The surrounding damage and local casualty assessment need separate confirmation.
Why early accounts differ
Several initial reports established only that nine people were aboard. Later coverage added Duffy’s confirmation that all nine died. That is a developing timeline, rather than evidence that nine people survived or that a passenger count was itself a death toll. Flight-tracking accounts also describe a steep descent, while some outlets discuss storms nearby. Neither observation establishes a cause. We are withholding exact descent speeds and unverified audio, and will report a cause only with clear attribution to findings or other substantiated evidence.
Jimmy’s Take
The first task here is straightforward: keep the reporting accurate as the facts develop. A video of the impact is powerful evidence of what people on the ground witnessed, but it leaves the central investigative question unanswered. We should be equally clear about what has been confirmed and what still requires an official answer. For now, the story is the loss of nine lives, an emergency response in a residential community and an investigation that has only begun. The next useful update will add verified information about the victims, people and property on the ground, or the sequence that led to the crash.

Nine killed as business jet crashes into South Florida neighbourhood
A business jet plunged into a South Florida neighbourhood on Sunday, killing all nine people aboard and exploding into a fireball near homes and a busy road. The pilot had reported icing, precipitation and severe turbulence before the Learjet entered a steep dive, according to air traffic control recordings.
A business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighbourhood Sunday and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway. Everyone on board was killed, the nation's transportation secretary said.
Video recorded by people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock that it landed only feet from homes and inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy posted on X that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County at 12:50 p.m. and called it a “horrific tragedy.” The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation, he said.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed.
Read moreItaly’s Ustica enigma: Can French files solve mystery crash blamed on stray missile?
“It was a cataclysmic plane crash,” DeSantis told reporters at the scene. “It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road.”
Rain pounded the region on Sunday. A flood watch due to excessive rainfall was in effect through Monday afternoon, the National Weather Service said.
The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
The plane was heading east at 35,000 feet (about 11 kilometres) when pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation and requested to climb 2,000 feet (about 610 metres).
Moments later, the plane entered a steep dive, first 10,000 feet per minute, then 20,000 feet per minute and up to 30,000 feet per minute, speeding the plane beyond its design limits, according to air traffic control recordings and flight tracking data.
A pilot declared an emergency and issued distress calls. The plane banked sharply to the right before it crashed steeply into the ground.
Read moreAmazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport, killing at least five
Minutes before the crash, the pilot reported ice accumulating on the jet and turbulence that was jolting it by as much as 700 feet, according to air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net.
“We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence,” the pilot told controllers.
But the situation rapidly deteriorated. After encountering precipitation and requesting to climb, the pilot declared an emergency as the aircraft began losing altitude at an alarming rate.
“We’re descending 8,000 – mayday, mayday - we’re descending 10,000 feet per minute,” the pilot radioed.
“We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute,” the pilot radioed, before delivering a devastating acknowledgement of what was about to happen. “We’re going to crash into the ground.”
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said the jet was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.
Palm Beach County authorities are evacuating about 600 people from a nearby mobile home community while federal officials investigate the crash. The road will be closed until further notice, county officials said.
(FRANCE 24 with AP)

WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — A business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway. Everyone on board was killed, the nation’s transportation secretary said.
Video recorded by people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock that it landed only feet from homes and inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy posted on X that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County at 12:50 p.m. and called it a “horrific tragedy.” The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation, he said.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed.
Trending
“It was a cataclysmic plane crash,” DeSantis told reporters at the scene. “It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road.”
Rain pounded the region on Sunday. A flood watch due to excessive rainfall was in effect through Monday afternoon, the National Weather Service said.
The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
The plane was heading east at 35,000 feet (about 11 kilometers) when pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation and requested to climb 2,000 feet (about 610 meters).
Moments later, the plane entered a steep dive, first 10,000 feet per minute, then 20,000 feet per minute and up to 30,000 feet per minute, speeding the plane beyond its design limits, according to air traffic control recordings and flight tracking data.
A pilot declared an emergency and issued distress calls. The plane banked sharply to the right before it crashed steeply into the ground.
Minutes before the crash, the pilot reported ice accumulating on the jet and turbulence that was jolting it by as much as 700 feet, according to air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net.
“We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence,” the pilot told controllers.
But the situation rapidly deteriorated. After encountering precipitation and requesting to climb, the pilot declared an emergency as the aircraft began losing altitude at an alarming rate.
“We’re descending 8,000 – mayday, mayday - we’re descending 10,000 feet per minute,” the pilot radioed.
“We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute,” the pilot radioed, before delivering a devastating acknowledgment of what was about to happen. “We’re going to crash into the ground.”
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said the jet was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.
Palm Beach County authorities are evacuating about 600 people from a nearby mobile home community while federal officials investigate the crash. The road will be closed until further notice, county officials said.
The crash occurred in Greenacres, Florida, according to Palm Beach County sheriff’s officials. The city of 45,000 people is about 7 miles (11 kilometers) southwest of West Palm Beach.
This story has been updated with further information on the location of the crash.

sources.news_title: All 9 people aboard a jet that crashed in Florida have died, transportation secretary says - The Boston Globe
sources.text:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — Parts of a business jet appear to have broken off before the aircraft crashed in South Florida and erupted into a ball of flames, killing all nine people on board, a federal investigator said Monday.
Video recorded by passersby captured the terrifying moment on Sunday afternoon when the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky before slamming into the ground and exploding in Greenacres, about 7 miles (11 kilometers) southwest of West Palm Beach. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as shocked residents looked on in horror. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
“Debris was everywhere. Debris hit my house. Everything was on fire. The road was on fire,” Anthony Blackmon, who lives near the crash site, told NBC affiliate WTVJ. “I’ve always seen it on the news, never thought it would happen so close to somebody like how it happened today.”
Federal investigators outline the probe but decline to speculate
National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman said during a news conference Monday that the aircraft appeared to start breaking up before it made impact and that he expects parts of the plane will be found far away.
“We do have some indication that the aircraft was breaking up before impact,” Chapman said. “We may find parts of the aircraft some distance away from the actual impact site.”
Aviation safety expert Jeff Guzzetti said key components of the jet’s tail may have been lost during the turbulence or as it nose-dived.
“If that happens you cannot control an airplane at that point. And that very well could explain the missile-like profile just before it hit the ground,” said Guzzetti, a former NTSB and the Federal Aviation Administration investigator.
Weather conditions will be a major focus of the investigation, Chapman said. Rain pounded the region on Sunday, and one of the pilots reported icing conditions at a high altitude in communications with air traffic control.
Weather radar maps from the time of the crash that FlightRadar24 combined with the plane’s flight path seem to show it flying directly into a storm cell that was rapidly expanding upward. But Chapman said investigators still have to determine what the weather conditions were at 35,000 feet.
Chapman said the plane was originally equipped with a cockpit voice recorder that investigators hope to recover.
“We have a lot of work to do on scene,” NTSB investigator Timothy Monville said at the news conference. “This will be a several-day process, and the biggest obstacle that we’re going to have is recovering the major wreckage from the impacted crater on the roadway.”
Mother identifies one of the pilots
The jet began its journey at the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas with two crew and seven passengers, Chapman said. Authorities have not released the names of the people who died and the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office declined to discuss the death investigation, which is ongoing.
Camila Corteleti told the New York Post and New York Times that her daughter, 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, was one of the pilots. She earned her pilot’s license in 2023 while a 17-year-old senior at West Boca Raton Community High School in Florida, local news reports said at the time.
Her pilot’s license showed she had the rating to fly that model of Learjet but not to be in command of the flight.
Her father, Allan Filgueiras, told The Associated Press he wasn’t prepared to speak about the crash.
A man who was driving close to the scene as the plane crashed suffered leg wounds, Monville said, but he didn’t know the extent of the injury.
Palm Beach County Mayor Sara Baxter asked for sympathy for the crash victims.
“Please keep them in your thoughts and prayers,” Baxter said.
Pilot reported turbulence and ice, then the jet’s rapid descent
The plane was heading east at 35,000 feet (11,000 meters) when the pilot started to report problems.
The pilot said ice was accumulating on the jet and that turbulence was jolting it by as much as 700 feet (213 meters), according to air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net. Rain pounded the region on Sunday.
“We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence,” the pilot told controllers.
Radar revealed thunderstorms with significant updrafts that would have pulled relatively warm moisture to the upper levels of the atmosphere, where large raindrops could have certainly frozen to the jet as it passed through a towering storm at around 40,000 feet, along with dramatically shifting wind speeds, according to meteorologists.
The situation rapidly deteriorated.
The pilot requested permission to climb another 2,000 feet (about 610 meters) and then quickly declared an emergency as the jet lost altitude at an alarming rate.
“We’re descending 8,000 — mayday, mayday — we’re descending 10,000 feet per minute,” the pilot radioed.
“We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute,” the pilot radioed. Moments later, the pilot said: “We’re going to crash into the ground.”
Video shows the plane banking sharply to the right before crashing and exploding.
Some area residents are still not allowed to return home
Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel G. Flores said at the news conference that the county “doesn’t have a clue” when residents who live near the crash site will be able to return to their homes as investigators continue to comb the area.
A shelter has been established for the residents of almost 80 mobile homes near the crash site, Flores said.
“Our concern right now is clearing the scene so that our residents can get back to normal,” he said. “We don’t really have a timeline as to when they are going to be able to comb through all the evidence and do everything they need to do, and that leaves our community looking for answers.”
___
Funk reported from Omaha, Nebraska. Associated Press writers Amy Taxin in Santa Ana, California; Dave Collins in Hartford, Connecticut; and Philip Marcelo in East Meadow, New York, contributed.
___
This story has been corrected to show the crash happened in Greenacres, not Green Acres.

“All northbound and southbound lanes of Military Trail are closed until further notice,” the sheriff’s office said. “Motorists are advised to avoid the area and seek alternate routes.”
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said the crash left a “big crater on the side of the road” and that there was debris everywhere as a result of the crash.
“This was a cataclysmic plane crash,” DeSantis said at a news conference. “It looked like a missile going down.”
As of Sunday evening, there were no reports of fatalities on the ground, DeSantis said.
Joel Flores, the Palm Beach County commissioner for District 3, said the priority is evacuating the about 600 people living in the area.
The Red Cross is on standby, he said.
The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to the scene to help the National Transportation Safety Board with its investigation, Duffy said.
Investigators with the NTSB will be arriving at the accident site Sunday and Monday morning.
A media briefing is planned in West Palm Beach for Monday, with a time and location pending, the NTSB said.
“Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost,” Duffy said.
This story is developing. Refresh for updates.

sources.news_title: Authorities investigating after plane crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida
sources.text:
Learjet crashes and erupts into flames in Florida, killing all 9 on board
By Cindy Von Quednow, Aaron Cooper, Pete Muntean, CNN
(CNN) — A private jet traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas careened into the ground in Palm Beach County, Florida, Sunday afternoon, leaving a deep crater and burning debris just feet from nearby homes and businesses and killing all nine on board, officials say.
Video from a passing vehicle shows the jet, a Learjet 60, slamming down nose first on a busy roadway in a flash before a fireball erupts.
“It was a cataclysmic plane crash,” Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said. “It looked like a missile going down.”
There were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured.
Before the crash, the pilot calmly reported ice accumulating on the aircraft, with an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius, and moderate turbulence, bouncing the plane by up to 700 feet, according to a recording of air traffic control radio calls captured by LiveATC.net.
But moments later, the pilot began to sound more panicked.
“Mayday, mayday,” the pilot told the Miami Air Route Traffic Control Center. “We’re descending 10,000 feet per minute!”
“We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute,” they yelled, “We’re going to crash into the ground!”
The jet descended 27,000 feet over the course of one minute, just before flight tracking data cut off, the website ADS-B Exchange shows.
Officials have not said what caused the jet to crash, and they have not identified the nine who died or said how many were passengers and crew.
There were scattered storms in the area at the time, and the plane passed through a stronger storm cell a few minutes before it began descending, but it is unclear if the storm contributed to the crash.
A news conference is expected Monday as authorities from the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board investigate.’
‘I heard and felt the boom’
The crash marks the second deadliest plane crash in the United States this year, according to NTSB records, after 12 people died in June when a skydiving plane crashed in Butler, Missouri. It is also the worst crash involving a Learjet 60, according to data from the Flight Safety Foundation. In 2008, four people were killed when a Learjet 60 bound for Los Angeles crashed on takeoff from Columbia, South Carolina.
The plane hit the ground shortly before 1 p.m. on Military Trail, a major thoroughfare between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office said. The roadway was left shattered and burning debris dotted the crater, video from CNN affiliate WPBF showed.
“There is a lot of debris that was strewn as a result of this crash,” DeSantis said.
The scene is just miles from the airport in West Palm Beach that was recently renamed for President Donald Trump and his Mar-A-Lago resort.
About 600 people are in need of shelter because the damage on the ground is blocking the entrance of a mobile home park, said Joel Flores, Palm Beach County commissioner for District 3, who was the first county official at the scene. Residents are being sent to two shelters in the county while the site is being investigated, he said.
“I heard and felt the boom,” Andrew Mannino told CNN. “The power immediately went out and is still out.”
Mannino said he smelled the smoke and “saw a large black cloud immerse in the air.”
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called the crash a “horrific tragedy.”
A steep descent
Dash cam video showing the crash is going to be important to investigators piecing together what happened, said Mary Schiavo, CNN aviation analyst and former inspector general for the Transportation Department.
“That is not a controlled descent,” Schiavo told CNN’s Fredricka Whitfield Sunday. “It’s clear, whatever happened, they had lost control of the plane.”
The steep descent could have forced parts of the plane to break off and the flight data recorder could have been destroyed in the explosion, she added.
Investigators will also have to piece together whether the environment played a part in the crash.
Ice on wings and other surfaces can also pose a major threat to private jets. In January 2024, the NTSB published a safety alert underscoring the risks of in-flight icing conditions, which can cause pilots to lose control. The agency warned ice can “make managing the airplane’s flightpath and airspeed more difficult and can prevent the airplane from maintaining level flight.”
It’s not clear if the plane had a cockpit voice recorder on board, but FAA regulations require jet aircraft with more than one engine to carry a voice recorder if they are flown for hire.
The plane is registered to an LLC in Delaware, according to FAA records, and is listed as available for charter online.
This story has been updated with additional information.

sources.news_title: Florida Learjet Crash Kills Nine as Residents Describe Massive Explosion That Shook Nearby Homes
sources.text:
Residents in Greenacres, Florida, have described the terrifying moments a business jet plunged from the sky and exploded on impact, killing all nine people aboard.
The crash happened at approximately 12.50pm on Sunday near the intersection of Military Trail and 10th Avenue North, close to West Palm Beach.
The $2 million Learjet 60 was travelling from Texas when it suddenly descended and struck the ground, triggering a huge fireball.
Family’s Apartment Shaken by Massive Explosion
A mother and her son were preparing to leave their apartment in Greenacres when they heard what the woman described as a ‘super big explosion’.
The impact was so powerful that their apartment began shaking, while the boy initially thought the noise was caused by an enormous lightning strike.
‘It sounded, like, very massive, huge,’ the mother told Fox News, explaining that her frightened son ran towards her immediately after hearing the blast.
She said the family subsequently lost electricity, while the curtains covering their windows began shaking.
Power was restored approximately seven minutes later.
When they looked outside, they noticed thick black smoke rising from the crash site before emergency sirens began sounding around three minutes later.
Other witnesses also reported feeling the force of the explosion, with some describing how they were lifted off the ground as the road began buckling and flames spread across the area.
DeSantis Compares Falling Jet to a Missile
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described the aircraft’s descent as he visited the crash site in heavy rain on Sunday evening.
‘When you see that video, you know, it’s a jarring thing,’ DeSantis said.
‘It was like… a missile coming down and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere.’
Dashcam footage captured the moment the aircraft plunged towards the ground before erupting into a massive fireball.
The impact created a large crater in the middle of the road and scattered aircraft debris across the surrounding area.
The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed that nine people were aboard the jet.
Authorities said no one on the ground was killed or injured.
Nearly 600 Residents Forced to Leave Their Homes
The crash has forced authorities to arrange temporary accommodation for nearly 600 residents of a nearby mobile home community.
The entrance to the neighbourhood is situated directly beside the wreckage, making it inaccessible while investigators examine the scene.
Former Greenacres Mayor and current Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores explained that residents could not remain in their homes because the entrance was part of the secured crash investigation area.
‘Unfortunately, that’s a crime scene. They’re investigating that, so the people can’t stay there,’ Flores said during a news conference.
County officials are preparing two shelters for those displaced, while the American Red Cross has been placed on standby.
The crash also damaged nearby infrastructure, raising concerns about possible disruptions to water and other essential services.
Damaged Road Could Remain Closed for a Month
Authorities do not expect the section of Military Trail affected by the crash to reopen within the next 30 days.
Flores said the investigation and repair work could keep the road closed for an extended period, while businesses in the surrounding area may also experience prolonged disruptions.
Federal investigators from the National Transportation Safety Board are examining the wreckage as they work to establish what caused the aircraft to crash.
Pilot Declared Emergency During Rapid Descent
Air traffic control recordings have provided details of the aircraft’s final moments before impact.
The Learjet was approaching the West Palm Beach area when controllers in Miami authorised the pilots to deviate left or right because of moderate precipitation to the southeast.
The weather was described as ‘pretty nasty’, with controllers subsequently reporting moderate turbulence.
The female pilot then informed air traffic control that the aircraft was rapidly descending.
‘Seven two two bravo delta, we’re descending 8,000… mayday mayday… we’re descending 10,000 ft per minute,’ she said.
Seconds later, she declared an emergency and reported that the aircraft was experiencing an overspeed condition.
‘Declaring emergency, declaring emergency we are in an overspeed condition,’ the pilot said before reporting that the jet was descending at 20,000 feet per minute.
Her voice became increasingly distressed as she warned that the aircraft was heading towards the ground.
‘I’m here with you, talk to me,’ the air traffic controller responded in an attempt to reassure her.
The pilot subsequently reported that the aircraft was descending at 22,000 feet per minute while banking at 60 degrees, indicating that its wings were tilted at a steep angle.
‘We’re out of time,’ she screamed.
The Daily Mail said it had chosen not to publish the final seconds of the recording because of their distressing nature.
Governor Says Something May Have Gone Wrong Midair
DeSantis later suggested that the aircraft may have experienced a serious problem before hitting the ground.
Asked about the jet’s rapid descent, the governor said its trajectory indicated that something had gone wrong while it was still airborne.
‘To see the way it descended, yeah, I think you can make the inference that something happened in the air that was a big problem,’ he said.
The precise cause of the crash has not been established.
Weather conditions in the West Palm Beach area were poor on Sunday afternoon, with overcast skies, rain and lightning reported in the vicinity.
Winds were blowing from the east at approximately 15mph, with gusts approaching 25mph.
The National Weather Service in Miami reported visibility of seven miles.
Flight Was Travelling From Texas to the Bahamas
Flight data showed that the aircraft had departed Austin, Texas, and was heading towards North Eleuthera in the Bahamas before its journey ended near West Palm Beach.
The crash occurred approximately eight miles from President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach.
Trump had been at the resort on Saturday evening, where he hosted hundreds of guests at a jungle-themed Halloween party.
The president attended the event dressed as himself, joking about his costume during his appearance.
‘I’ve spent nine hours getting ready. I had ten minutes, so I came as Donald Trump tonight! Hello everybody,’ he said.
By Sunday, as the aircraft crashed near West Palm Beach, Trump had travelled to Iowa for the final stage of his midterm election campaign.

Business Jet Crash in South Florida Claims Nine Lives
South Florida, November 2: A tragic incident occurred in South Florida on Sunday when a business jet crashed into a residential area, resulting in the deaths of all nine passengers on board. Eyewitness videos captured the moment the jet transformed into a fireball upon impact, engulfing the area in thick black smoke.
The crash took place near Cresthaven in Palm Beach County. Reports indicate that the aircraft narrowly missed colliding with nearby homes, which could have resulted in even more casualties. However, it still landed on a busy road, causing a loud explosion upon impact. Images and videos from the scene show widespread chaos as emergency responders rushed to the area.
This devastating accident has raised concerns about air safety and the potential risks posed by private jets operating in residential zones. Investigations are underway to determine the cause of the crash and to ensure the safety of air travel in the future.
